title: Why does circling and crossing out find only primes?
description: Leeza and Ruhee wonder why the sieve gives only primes, and the board follows what happens to a circled number and to a crossed out number. Keeko doubts that there is a reason and says that the sieve works by magic.
teaching_notes: One idea: a crossed out number is a multiple of a smaller number, so it has an extra factor, and a circled number was never crossed out, so it has no extra factor. Watch for students who treat the sieve as a trick that has no reason.

source: Leeza and Ruhee started wondering how this simple method is a
video_script.why: The child sees that crossing out a multiple gives it an extra factor, and that a circled number escaped every crossing, so it has only one and itself as factors.
video_script.substitution: Look at what happens to one crossed out number and one circled number.
video_script.anchor: The finished table of the numbers from 1 to 100 with circled and crossed out numbers
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the sieve works by magic. Seven stayed circled because three, five and the other smaller numbers could not divide it, and fifteen was crossed out because three divides it, so each result has a reason.
video_script.payoff_line: Circled numbers have exactly two factors, so they are prime. Crossed out numbers have more, so they are composite.

final_answer.value: circled numbers have exactly two factors, so they are prime; crossed-out numbers have more, so they are composite
final_answer.spoken: the sieve circles primes and crosses out composites

maths_rules: 15 is crossed out in the round of 3 because 15 = 3 × 5, so 15 has the factors 1, 3, 5, 15
when 7 is reached it is not crossed out: the multiples of 2, 3 and 5 are already crossed out and 7 is not one of them
multiples of 4 and 6 are multiples of 2 or 3, so they were crossed out earlier
so no number from 2 to 6 divides 7, and 7 has only the factors 1 and 7
a crossed out number has the factor of its round besides 1 and itself, so it has more than 2 factors
video_script.design: One crossed out number (15) and one circled number (7) are followed round by round on the finished table.
